messages:
ashley: Thanks everyone — quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A about reviews/promos/comp. If you asked a question live or want clarification, drop it here and I'll answer or link the policy. I'll also paste the updated timeline below. :memo:

devin: Are promotion effective dates always the first of the month? wondering about retro pay for May promos.

ashley: Short answer: not always, but most salary changes hit the first payroll after the comp letter. We try to make promo effective dates align to the 1st of the month for payroll simplicity. Retro pay is applied when promos are effective mid-cycle — HR runs a retro calc. :calendar:

kelly: Can you confirm when comp letters go out? I want to make sure managers know the comms plan.

ashley: Comp letters -> manager review: May 18. Letters sent to managers: May 20. Managers have until May 27 to acknowledge and start 1:1s. Company-wide email to recipients targeted for May 28.

jordan: For calibration, how heavily are comp bands vs role scope weighted? We've had folks hit level expectations but still get small bumps.

ashley: Calibration rubric weighs scope/impact ~60% and comp band positioning ~40% for salary decisions. Promotions require demonstrating level competencies; comp adjustments can be band-driven. I'll share the rubric excerpt below.

ashley: ```
Calibration priorities:
1) Role/impact evidence (work examples, metrics) - ~60%
2) Market/band position - ~25%
3) Internal equity / comp balance - ~15%
```

tanvi: Does parental leave count toward last-cycle impact? e.g., someone who was on leave for 10 weeks — how do managers present that?

ashley: Managers are explicitly asked to include leave context in calibration packets. Time on leave is not penalized; focus is on demonstrated impact in the measured window. We added an optional "context" field to the packet form.

sam: Is there any chance of mid-cycle (ad-hoc) promos for high-performers before this main cycle? Or do we wait until the formal cycle?

ashley: We still approve off-cycle promos for exceptional cases, but we ask managers to reserve them for truly urgent moves. Off-cycle promos often trigger a separate comp review and may have different timing for pay changes.

devin: Where's the canonical doc? Can we get a link to share with our teams?

hr-bot: Posted: https://redwood.internal/hr/reviews/2026-spring-timeline (internal-only). Attachment preview: "Review packet updates, manager checklist, and comp letter templates." :link:

ashley: Copying the key dates here for visibility:
- May 10-14: Manager calibration week
- May 18: Manager review deadlines
- May 20: Comp letters to managers
- May 27: Manager ack & 1:1s start
- June 1: Pay adjustments effective (for promos effective on 1st)

kelly: Thanks. One last ask — can we get anonymized breakdowns of promotion rates by level for last cycle? leadership asked me for data.

ashley: Yes — I'll request the anonymized export from People Ops analytics and post in this thread when ready (no PII). ETA ~ 48 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jordan: Appreciated. Also if anyone needs a manager guide doc for running calibration sessions, ping me and I'll share the template I use.

ashley: Great — thank you! I'll close with: please point any manager-level questions to me or drop them here and we'll coordinate a short office hour next week for managers doing calibrations. :raised_hands:
